subject: physical-education

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of walking, hiking, cycling, and self-paced endurance activity in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe strength, mobility, and bodyweight practice using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply yoga, stretching, and mindful movement in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving racket, throwing, and precision activities for two; correct it and explain why.
Connect access: cost, equipment, location, and time as real constraints with trialing an activity honestly before judging it and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Trial three individual or dual activities, evaluate each against enjoyment, access, cost, and sustainability, and justify which one is worth continuing.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Individual and Dual Lifetime Activities?
